name: 115. raw_request on the embedding success path (bedrock + vertex) (embedding-raw-request)
description:
Bedrock and Vertex embeddings reported `extra_fields.raw_request` on every error return but never on success. Both hand-roll their response unmarshal rather than calling `HandleProviderResponseCtx` — Bedrock because the response struct differs per model family (Titan / Cohere / Nova), Vertex because it differs per endpoint (`:predict` / `:embedContent`) — and when that was written only the response half was carried over. The result: with `x-bf-send-back-raw-request: true`, a failing embedding call returned the request bytes and a succeeding one silently dropped them.

Every other embedding path already did this — OpenAI (via the shared `HandleOpenAIEmbeddingRequest`), Cohere and Gemini all set it — so these two were the outliers, not the rule.

The fix is the established `providerUtils.ParseAndSetRawRequest` (56 call sites), which stores the body as a compacted `json.RawMessage` so the exact bytes and key order survive. 115.A1 asserts that ordering directly, since a decode through `map[string]interface{}` would sort the keys and that is precisely what the helper exists to avoid.

Three Bedrock rows rather than one because Titan, Cohere and Nova unmarshal down three separate branches of the same switch and the capture sits after it — one family passing says nothing about the others. Each row also checks the reported body is the **converted provider envelope** (`inputText`, `taskType`, `texts[]`, `instances[]`), not the OpenAI-dialect request that arrived. Run with FEATURE=embedding-raw-request.

item.name: 115.A Bedrock embedding raw_request, across all three model families
115.A1 bedrock/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 - raw_request is reported on a successful embedding

exec: // Pins that raw_request survives the embedding success path on Bedrock (Titan family).
var txt = pm.response.text() || '';
pm.test('embedding succeeds', function () {
pm.expect(pm.response.code, 'failed: ' + txt.slice(0, 300)).to.eql(200);
var body; try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) {
pm.expect.fail('response was not JSON: ' + txt.slice(0, 300)); return; }
// The embedding path unmarshals per model family instead of going through
// HandleProviderResponse, and used to report raw_request only on the error returns -
// so a successful call silently dropped it while a failing one carried it.
var rr = (body.extra_fields || {}).raw_request;
pm.test('raw_request is reported on a successful embedding', function () {
pm.expect(rr, 'raw_request missing - x-bf-send-back-raw-request is honored on errors but not on success: ' + txt.slice(0, 300)).to.not.be.undefined;
pm.expect(rr, 'raw_request present but null').to.not.be.null;
// The provider body is Titan's own envelope, not the OpenAI request that came in: proof the
// converted bytes are what gets reported, and that key order survives (inputText before
// dimensions is the order the converter emits; a map decode would sort them the other way).
pm.test('it carries the converted Titan body, key order intact', function () {
var asText = typeof rr === 'string' ? rr : JSON.stringify(rr);
pm.expect(asText, 'not the Titan envelope: ' + asText.slice(0, 200)).to.include('inputText');
pm.expect(asText, 'dimensions did not reach the provider body').to.include('dimensions');
pm.expect(asText.indexOf('inputText'), 'key order was not preserved').to.be.below(asText.indexOf('dimensions'));
pm.expect(asText, 'the OpenAI-dialect field name leaked into the provider body').to.not.include('"input"');
